newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Both in-laws of Yeltsin doctor killed.
newsitem.headline: Both in-laws of Yeltsin doctor killed.

text.p: The mother-in-law and the father-in-law of a doctor who treats Russian President Boris Yeltsin have both been found killed, police said on Wednesday.

A police spokesman said the father-in-law, Andrei Ichko, was found dead with a skull fracture early on Wednesday. His body was discovered in the stairwell of the apartment block where his wife Anna was stabbed to death one day before.

Public Russian Television (ORT) said on Tuesday that relatives nearly caught one of Anna Ichko's attackers, but the assailant jumped off the balcony of the apartment as the relatives tried to open the front door.
An investigator told the television the incident looked like a robbery and appeared to have no political motive.
ORT said the couple were the parents of the wife of doctor Vladlen Vtorushin, who has been treating Yeltsin for two years.
"Vladlen Vtorushin is a strong man. He will be able to cope with this tragedy and there is no need to replace him," it quoted Sergei Mironov, head of the Kremlin medical centre, as saying on Tuesday.
But the ORT anchorwoman recalled that a personal doctor of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was killed earlier this year.
"A natural question arises -- maybe now, ahead of the president's operation, we should not make public the names of those who would carry it out?" the presenter said.

Yeltsin, 65, Russian leader said on September 5 that he would have heart surgery. He spent almost four weeks in hospital from September 13 while doctors got him ready for surgery and moved to the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow this weekend.
Russian heart surgeon Renat Akchurin is expected to lead the operation, likely in the next two months.
